stem:
Adil compares a mixture of iron filings and sulfur with iron sulfide formed by heating them.

Which claims correctly describe the mixture before heating? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Yellow sulfur grains and dark iron particles can both still be seen.
A magnet can attract the iron from the mixture.
The mixture is already a compound because two substances sit together.
The mixture has one uniform black colour and is never magnetic.

teacher.key_rationale: Before heating, iron and sulfur keep separate appearance and magnetism. Calling any two substances together a compound, or giving the mixture the compound's uniform non-magnetic look, misses the mixture-versus-compound hinge.
